messages.text:
Hey. Sorry it's a bit late in the day, but here's the feedback.

*CONFESSION BOX*
• We like this format. Love how it’s centred around real dilemmas from young men.
• The Vox Pop element also brings in real young men’s experiences in an interesting way too.
• We could also think about how we get the questions – do we write them ourselves, but eventually source them from the YT comments to create engagement, for example.
*Considerations*
• *The rationale for the park*
    ◦ Is the primary reason for this to differentiate from more studio-based / podcast style discussion shows? Or is it to facilitate the Vox Pops?
    ◦ We like how it feels like a space that young men hang out and feels relatable to them, but could the park limit the global appeal (if it’s set in a British park could it put off Aussie audience?). We’ll need to consider this alongside talent.
    ◦ Would it make more sense to separate the talent discussion from the Vox pops which could mean we could shoot vox pops in different parks In key markets (could get our local content teams to help with this if needed).
    ◦ Is setting it in a park adding an unnecessary logistical layer that adds complexity and budget and do we think the pros outweigh these cons (e.g. capturing sound is always quite tricky in a park and you have to think about weather). 
• *Experts*
    ◦ How do we weave in experts / expert advice
• *Talent*
    ◦ Do we think it’s the same talent or a host + a guest each time?
    ◦ Is there a way to bring in global voices so it feels less localised? Or do we think it’s better to keep it authentic to one market to create engagement. To discuss.
*OUT OF BOUNDS*
• We were less keen on this because it feels more difficult to centre this one on relationships and also bring in some of the advice we want to give.
• This approach is similar to what we briefed for the <https://uk.movember.com/story/top-youtubers-partner-with-movember-to-support-young-men|YouTuber series> we did. All the creators took a different journey, and with some of them it felt like the conversation was crowbarred in a bit! E.g. <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-oJziE9El00>
• It feels like with this one we would be making life difficult for ourselves as we’d need new topics and also new challenges with each episode and weave them together - potentially more entertaining, but it could take the focus away from the topic. And given we know guys are looking for info on this, do we need to add another entertainment layer in this way?
• It’s also quite difficult to do this in a way which feels global as the challenges by their nature will always be interacting with the local environment.

messages.text: Really nice!

Hello TNM team.

We had a catch up earlier with Ben, who heads up comms and social at Movember, regarding the YouTube channel.

He is fairly new in the role and has just been developing a new social operations model for Movember. He’s well aware that the existing YouTube channel is a bit of a dumpng ground and it’s mainly used for dark posting content.

The plan is ultimately for Movember to start developing content which resonates much more with users seeking inspiration or practical knowledge on health topics, grounded in SEO learnings. This is a bit down the priority list for his team, but it's in the plan for next year.

Ben suggested that we almost need to assume we’re starting from zero with the existing channel, and given YouTube is pretty search driven (and people don’t tend to subscribe to brands, they are more likely to search for content), wouldn’t it make sense to use the Movember channel to publish our content – so we’re not then cannibalising our own content in future which will also be aimed at young men.

He said we could think about what we might need to do to the existing channel to ready it for our content.

 I feel like this is a very valid suggestion given this longer-term strategy, but I’m thinking it might limit the content views given the algorithm does serve new content to subscribers and many of them won’t be young men?

I wanted to get your perspective and suggest we get a couple of you on a Slack thread with Ben so we can work it through together?

Ultimately I think we need to do what’s gong to be best for the audience, but if we’re able to align it with longer term social team goals without jeopardising that, then I’m all for it.

messages.text:
Hey Tom

Thanks again for the insight and questions. These are always tricky equations but we're very confident there will be little to no cannibalisation of Movember's existing Youtube channel with this content, and won't be seen as repetitive as you'd be reaching completely different audiences. For some more context, we've collated some examples of young channels garnering loads of views and engagement without the existing subscriber base to match:

• <https://www.youtube.com/@Money-Match|Money Match>, a channel with just one upload — an explainer about the economics of Manchester United has already hit 100k views with fewer than 100 subscribers. It’s a reminder that YouTube rewards specificity and strong audience alignment — even without a pre-existing subscriber base.
• <https://www.youtube.com/@survivehistory|Survive History> which has a large subscriber base now, was getting huge views with very few subscribers about a year ago (we have a relationship with the creator behind the channel so have the knowledge base here).
• <https://www.youtube.com/@NinjaFitnessPrankTV|Ninja Fitness Prank TV> has 4.4k subscribers and with 54 videos is only 1 month old. It's first ever video has amassed 844k views, with all posted since pulling in great numbers. Content-first approach is key, with consistent runtime, edit style, thumbnail design, and the same format each time, not deviating to other formats. This is a fan account which re-edits <https://www.youtube.com/@vladimirfitness/videos|another creator's> content, which although not great practice if it isn't in collaboration with the creator, the case study demonstrates that you can grow a channel really quick when there's a niche format featuring *famous and recognisable faces*, which we intend to do with our new channel by featuring popular creators, rappers and artists with our target young male audience
It's worth noting that posting on both the new and existing channels would also be an option given the low risk on cannibalisation. It'll also be trickier to revive an existing channel while pushing to a completely separate audience. Would very likely  require a bit of heavier lift as the content now is focused on docu-style testimonial content.

The Movember main channel could absolutely benefit from a clear editorial shift: niching down and creating smart, entertaining content tailored to young men. But turning that vision into reality (while building real momentum behind it) would take a considerably larger amount of time, and getting it off the ground before the TNM x Movember pilot goes live would be tight.

From our experience, successfully pivoting a channel would involve:
	•	Auditing the existing subscriber base and viewing habits
	•	Privating or unlisting older content that no longer fits
	•	Rebranding with new visual identity, content pillars, and upload cadence
	•	Resetting audience expectations and letting the algorithm adapt

In short - it's doable but wanted to make you aware of the strategic and operational lift involved and flag the risks of short-term underperformance as we navigate both the audience and the algorithm with the new style of content.

Hopefully all makes sense but happy to chat anything through if you need! Any Qs / elaboration needed please just shout.

Sorry for the delay, Tom! Hopefully the below is helpful. Any more Qs let us know - otherwise have a great weekend!

On Youtube, you're right. Content get's served to a small group of users, typically 1) subscribers, 2) users who've clicked on and watched your content recently, and 3) users who watch similar content with shared keywords in the title, tags, and description. If your channel is big with hundreds of thousand of subscribers, this initial test group is tens of thousands of people. If it is small, i.e hundred of subscribers, it will likely be around 1-10,000 people. The algorithm then decides if your content should be pushed more broadly through 2 key analytics, impression click through rate % (how many people clicked the thumbnail to watch), and average view duration (how long they stayed to watch). Therefore, YouTube depends a lot on people consciously clicking and making a choice to watch the episode.

Tiktok is different, because it's an autoplay feed, the content lives and dies by the opening couple of seconds. It’s a content-first platform, similarly shown to an initial test group made up of users who have watched similar content in their last few sessions on Tiktok. The algorithm prioritises what people have recently watched and engaged with — not who they follow. It's easier to pivot a channel because of this, as your not having to please existing subscribers are people who liked your last video formats. That means a great cutdown from a new YouTube series can still perform well on the Movember TikTok, even if the full series isn’t hosted there.

We would recommend posting some clips on Movember as it's your main voice of activity across the charity, and would have good chance of getting views, however we would still recommend creating a new Tiktok to post these cutdowns/clips on in addition to on the Movember main channel. Sorry for the delay, Tom! Hopefully the below is helpful. Any more Qs let us know - otherwise have a great weekend!

On Youtube, you're right. Content get's served to a small group of users, typically 1) subscribers, 2) users who've clicked on and watched your content recently, and 3) users who watch similar content with shared keywords in the title, tags, and description. If your channel is big with hundreds of thousand of subscribers, this initial test group is tens of thousands of people. If it is small, i.e hundred of subscribers, it will likely be around 1-10,000 people. The algorithm then decides if your content should be pushed more broadly through 2 key analytics, impression click through rate % (how many people clicked the thumbnail to watch), and average view duration (how long they stayed to watch). Therefore, YouTube depends a lot on people consciously clicking and making a choice to watch the episode.

Tiktok is different, because it's an autoplay feed, the content lives and dies by the opening couple of seconds. It’s a content-first platform, similarly shown to an initial test group made up of users who have watched similar content in their last few sessions on Tiktok. The algorithm prioritises what people have recently watched and engaged with — not who they follow. It's easier to pivot a channel because of this, as your not having to please existing subscribers are people who liked your last video formats. That means a

great cutdown from a new YouTube series can still perform well on the Movember TikTok, even if the full series isn’t hosted there.

We would recommend posting some clips on Movember as it's your main voice of activity across the charity, and would have good chance of getting views, however we would still recommend creating a new Tiktok to post these cutdowns/clips on in addition to on the Movember main channel. Hey all. Thanks for the catch up last week and the discussion on how we integrate experts. Sharing for your reference <@U07S9KV4VGR>.

I agree with you that route A makes most sense. Feedback from our end:
• With route B, I don’t think we can have the expert as host – my feeling is we need to have some pulling power from someone who already has a presence in culture. Not saying all of our audiences across each market need to know the talent, but I think we need something which gives us some cultural credibility and helps us build an audience.
• With route C, this style feels a bit too removed from the overall format style, and I think if we go down this route, we risk the expert bit being seen as a bolt-on or at worst it feels a bit blander or serious and it puts the audience off watching the advice from the expert.
• Route A feels good – it means we have talent leading and discussing the scenario, and we bring in other voices (real young people) + experts in a way which feels like it could work.
The only I'd have if whether this complicates the park setting? As you’d potentially have the talent discussing in a park, vox pops shot somewhere else, and expert shot in another place.

And when it comes to the host would be still looking for a host who is discussing the scenario with another person, e.g. someone like Ben Hurst (a soft expert as you say)

Hi TNM team, one of our research partners (The Good Side) is putting on an event Labs Live: Marketing Meets The Manosphere with BBH on the manosphere and asked if some from your team might be interested in coming? It's a little late notice, but let us know if anyone is keen and we can get you on the list!

*Thursday 19th June from 8.30 - 10.30am at 60 Kingly St, Soho*

As part of its new Labs Live series,  *BBH* will be joined by experts from *The Good Side, Movember* and the *BBC* to dive into the manosphere, and explore how influencer culture is reshaping notions of masculinity, why this content engages young men, and the crucial role brands play in crafting a new narrative.
BBH will host an exclusive screening of the documentary short *‘Influenced: The Online Masculinity Map’* which tells the real-life story of Will Adolphy, a former red-piller turned therapist, and reveal insights from The Good Side’s two year research study with Movember about what motivates and engages young male audiences online.
This will be followed by a panel discussion, hosted by *BBH CSO Will Lion* alongside *Saul Parker, CEO of The Good Side, Sarah Sternberg, Director for Reimagining Masculinities at Movember* and *Jo Hudson, Head of TV Audience at BBC,* where they will discuss how brands can rewrite the script and be part of the solution in rethinking what modern masculinity means.

messages.text:
Hey! YouTube doesn’t love it when you post the _exact_ same video on two different channels (can hurt reach). It will deprioritise what it believes to be an exact duplicate. Best workaround is to tweak the second upload slightly — change the intro/outro, use a different title/thumbnail, and space out the uploads by a few days. We could also tailor the framing: more charity-focused on Movember’s main channel (Real Talk with Young Men), and more punchy/entertainment-first on the new one (Loski did WHAT to his first girlfriend??!)

Another consideration is hosting all the videos on the new channel and then embedding a playlist on the home page of the main Movember channel. You're not then splitting views between two places, but have visibility on the main Movember channel.

<@U044N07QC7P> <@U08PJULDVF1> thanks for agreeing to do the internal session on Monday.

So for context this is a meeting we have every couple of months with our wider young men's health portfolio team. So it includes people that work across our other initiatives in sport / gaming & esports / masculinities. Plus we open it to other relevant people from research / advocacy / fundraising / marketing.

The purpose is to update a wider group who aren't as aware of the work and we often bring a partner in so they can get exposure to all the great people we're working with. The last session was the gaming team with it's <https://about.blast.tv/> talking about their mental health work in esports. It's a pretty friendly session where people will ask questions to understand the work and approach a bit more.

It's 1 hour and suggested approach is:

• TNM to do a short overview deck of who they are (you could use the pitch deck intro or something else if you'd prefer) - 10mins
• Tom present the approach (I'll do a cutdown of this document I used for an internal meeting the other day) - 15mins
• Q&A which Harry will host, and I've given him some questions to ask us to kick off 
    ◦ How do we hope impact young men's mental health through this work? 
    ◦ Do we really think we can reach young guys and engage them in healthy relationships content. 
    ◦ Why are we using YouTube? 
    ◦ What’s the role of talent in this? 
    ◦ How will we ensure the content is engaging to young men? 
    ◦ Plus any questions from the group
Does that sound ok?

messages.text:
I don't think we'll monetise the channel as it's probably too risky given the audience we're going for that we end up with adverts for diet pills or dodgy AI companions next to the content.

Usage rights - I'd be keen to hear your thoughts on what a host might want. I think we'd want to fully own the usage, and we want to create content that has an evergreen feel so probably want to negotiate long-term usage / usage in perpituity.

In terms of affiliate usage, I think ultimately we'd want to have the option of getting a brand on board to co-fund the content and this would probably look like a brand sponsorship of the channel, with potentially option to create some specials (e.g. we did <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Cclps1lnCic|this> with The Overlap and Gillette last year).

If the hosts wanted usage to use content on their own channels, we could think about that.

Not sure if that answers all your questions. Keen to hear your perspective on any of this as we've got some flex on all of this.

<@U02QB9QJHGQ> Thanks so much for the information — super helpful. Great point regarding the unpredictable nature of YouTube ads.
With talent of this caliber (which is really exciting!), higher rates are expected, particularly to safeguard their name and likeness. Based on the sensitivity around usage and ownership, I’d like to propose the following:
• *Ownership*: _In perpetuity_, given the primary objective is to build the channel’s reach and long-term content library. Content lives on channel in perpetuity. 
• *Paid Usage*: _1 year to start_, to align with standard talent agreements.
• *Affiliate Usage*: _3 months_, as talent typically charges monthly for these types of partnerships. Starting with a shorter period allows us to monitor performance before expanding.

Hey Courtney. Can I just clarify a few bits here.

I wanted to understand how we're thinking about the ownership and paid usage and make sure I'm clear on how we're defining it.

*Ownership:* my understanding is that this relates to the channel + format + any content on there. So essentially saying that we are paying to own the episodic content on the channel and then have it remaining there. And we'd have to build this into the host contracts + all guest talent featuring?

*Paid usage:* relates to using content for paid promotion & advertising. So we'd be able to use it to promote channel for 1 year and then if we wanted to continue using a specific talent's content to promote, we'd need to strike a new agreement.

*Affiliate usage:* is about getting the talent to promote on their own channels?

Can you confirm this or let me know if I'm misunderstanding!

The other bits I think I just want to make sure we're considering:

• *Future channel sponsorship:* if we get a sponsor to fund some of the content in future (e.g. think about a commercial youth brand like JD or Lynx) do we need to build anything in that considers this?
• *Movember channel usage:* We might want to use snippets of the content in Movember reels / Movember website / Movember social posts. Do we need to build anything in to cover this?

slackdump_thread_replies.text: Correct!

Just on the legal side, I spoke to our legal team and they said:

As you know, under our MSA with The News Movement (NM) we own any IP generated from the deliverables in our SoW. If TNM uses third parties to complete any of the these deliverables, then it's their obligation to ensure that they have the right arrangements in place to ensure that they can ultimately assign the IP rights to Movember. I have copied the relevant clause below (with the specific section in noted in bold).

_5.1 The Parties agree that all right, title and interest in and to any Contract IP are the exclusive property of Movember. To give effect to this clause 5.1, the Service Provider *must execute all such documents and do all such acts as Movember may reasonably require*._

We therefore don't have to necessarily review their third party contracts. But I am happy to review their template if you think  there is value and that it will give us comfort. Have you spoken to TNM about the need to ensure that IP rights from their third party contracts can be assigned to Movember at the end?

Hey *<!channel>* - thanks again for providing the first round of ideas on series name / channel name / logo style.
Please find the Creative studio team at Movember thought's below:

*Channel name:* MO TV
*Series name:* Favourite - Confession Box / Alts - Confessions / Unfiltered / Between two flags / DM's - See rationale in attached doc
*Logos - Options in order of preference - and a request to explore another territory:*
1. The Wildcard - option 5 - based on what was provided
2. Font and style of version 1 for 'confessions' - combined with font and style version 2 for 'box'.
3. Can you please explore an alt that feels more lo-fi - real and 'anti-perfect' in line with what's trending for Gen Zs - whether it’s scrawled with a marker or written as a death metal font or sign written with bright colours that will feel more down to earth...
When sending these new versions, please include ‘Grown by Movember' underneath as this will be mandatory :slightly_smiling_face:

I've attached the notes from the creative studio team so you can see the other options circulated and thoughts behind it, in case you want to deliberate more, but otherwise feel we're all landing in a similar place.

Also a future request for when you present storyboards, can you please include a mock up of the supers leveraging Overpass please?

Look forward to hearing your thoughts / seeing the next round of designs. Thanks!

messages.text:
Thanks for flagging <@U03KNV84NUB> – totally understand your concern. We’ve been exploring multiple parks across London as we feel a park backdrop allows these conversations to feel open, natural and authentic, as opposed to a studio environment. I take your point on Kew potentially reading as a bit “prim”, but we landed on this shot because it strikes a nice balance: it feels open and public without leaning into overly stylised or try-hard territory (like a skatepark or football pitch might). The specific location we chose feels anonymous - there are no real signifiers, and there is a great depth of field to add some depth to our shot. It would be extremely hard to identify this as Kew unless you knew, and we think that's good.

It's also worth saying that we'll be shooting the vox pop segment in a different location - busier, more urban parks, and capturing b-roll of general park life - skateboarding, chatting, walking, etc.

Ultimately, we believe that the relatability for our target audience will come from the talent, titling, thumbnails and, most importantly, the confessions themselves – with the location serving as a subtle, neutral backdrop.

And, there is strong creative research around thumbnail design. Bright, high‑contrast colours like green work particularly well—they stand apart from YouTube’s dominant red/white/black interface, which improves visibility and Click-through-rate. Green will be the background for each thumbnail, with the talent taking centre stage.

messages.text:
Hey <@U03KNV84NUB> & team. Again, thanks for reviewing our latest suggestions so quick - really helps us keep things moving fast. We’ve connected as a team today and chatted through your feedback. Take a look at our thoughts below

*Logos*

To confirm, You prefer *No. 2 logo,* using Owners and Modak fonts. <@U09104V5VR9> will work on adding the “Grown By Movember” slogan to this option in line with your brand guidelines. She'll send this over tomorrow, then later this week she will get to work on colour variations and a stacked variation, all using the Grown By Movember line.

*Props*

Throughout this pitching and pre-production process, we’ve watched a lot of similar Youtube content aimed at Gen Z Men on Youtube. I’ve <https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/10E0gANnDrma7Z5b04cod3NXfaEWEbbVodyJj5ecpf8s/edit?usp=sharing|collated some of the biggest vodcast setups here>, where setups can range from looking like a family living room (Siedcast) to what looks like Stephen Fry’s attic (UnProvoked on GRM Daily)! In our opinion, talent is king. If cool names are in it and the format is simple and entertaining, it’s a strong recipe regardless of the furniture/set. But, we do hear your concerns about the current mockup  - and we like your suggestion for a more rough-around-the-edges, second hand aesthetic. We’d suggest two mismatched second hand leather armchairs on top of a more worn-out looking red rug. We’ve attached the options. What do you think? These options are on marketplace sites so they may go quickly, but for now they'll help us agree the vision! Keen to hear your thoughts.

I Hope this makes sense, and feel free to get back your team's thoughts in this chain tomorrow. We also have our weekly status call with Tom, Tess and Harry tomorrow at 3pm - 3.45pm UK time if you or anyone on your team want to jump in to chat things through. Let me know if you want an invite! Thanks :pray:

messages.text:
*Hi all,*
Thanks so much for the consolidated feedback <@U03KNV84NUB> — super helpful to get the brand team’s thoughts in one place. We’ve discussed internally and wanted to share our considered responses before we jump into another round of mock‑ups:
*Logo:*
• We’ll mock up the ‘Grown by Movember’ sizing adjustments for legibility and show you a revised stacked version with a smaller ‘Box’.
• For clarity: our recommendation is that ‘Grown by Movember’ features on the *channel logo, header and all PR/media assets*, but *not on the thumbnail logo* (where clarity at small sizes is key, and the thumbnail is just to small to make it legible on mobile).
• Chloe will also explore alternative tweaks that achieve contrast while keeping visibility strong on dark/light backgrounds - for example, the stroke on the yellow mockup.
*Chairs:*
• Understood on preferring mismatched/second‑hand — we really like <https://www.wayfair.co.uk/furniture/pdp/rosdorf-park-penermon-72cm-wide-armchair-lvfs1764.html?piid=86677528|this one> you sent over as it balances style & masculinity with enough comfort for guests (as comfort will help create more open conversations).
• We’ll provide a couple of chairs along this route, prioritising buying second hand, but we do want to raise the point that availability/delivery may lead us to buying from retailers rather than off Facebook Marketplace etc
*Plinth:*
• We’d recommend keeping a stylised plinth like this one as the Confession Box centerpiece, as YouTube sets still need a strong stylistic anchor. We believe his piece gives the set a more dramatic, streetwear‑inspired focal point, adding a layer of design that elevates the overall look while keeping the Box as the visual heart of the show.
• We have looked at cool, chunky coffee tables prevously but a lot of them are a bit too low (35cm Height) so the box will be around knee level, and the talent will be reaching down to grab into it, which we fear may look a bit unnatural. We think the best bet is a narrow side table that the box snugly fits on top of, at around 50cm height.
• However, we do understand your point and we've explored similar side‑table options to soften the look while keeping the function and centerpiece quality. Let us know your thoughts on them (attached). 
*Box:*
• We’d strongly recommend keeping the logo on the box — without it, it risks looking like a random prop rather than the anchor of the series.
• Also, alot of our audience will perhaps see the content via our amplification partners (i.e brands reposting cutdowns and clips on Tiktok and Instagram), so having the logo instantly explains to them that this is a recurring format on Youtube, that they can go and find by searching "Confession Box".
• That said, if there’s a concern about it feeling “too branded,” we’d love to hear your ideas on *alternative ways to carry branding through the set* so the series still feels visually owned.
• An interesting case study is the *<https://www.youtube.com/@OfficialFlagrant|FLAGRANT>* podcast, one of the most popular male-podcasts in the US, which started with a heavily branded set to gain momentum and recognition when shared beyond Youtube, like in Tiktok clips and Instagram Reels. Now they have a huge following, It's since scaled back and has no branding on set. So we feel that to launch the show, the box should have the logo on to help make this the start of a longstanding Youtube show!
*Rug:*
• Great — we’ll keep as is.
I think we're almost there with this, let us know your steer on the table and we'll hope to get things locked in by Friday.
Thanks again for the detailed feedback — we’ll keep you posted

messages.text:
Hi <@U03KNV84NUB> and team - circling back on some questions you had outstanding logo/design details:

I totally agree about using black and white for the logo to be consistent (I think the B/w version is strongest but wanted you to see the color variations incase) and we can just use mustard as a secondary color in other ways. I'll make sure to shrink the word "BOX" on the stacked logo variation (just need to keep the proportions vertical so that it doesn't just become another horizontal variation if you know what I mean).

I think the best next step is for me to mock up some guidelines and assets so we can get into the details, and also see the bigger picture of it all coming together. If your team can give me the thumbs up on the below list, I'll get you a comprehensive brand guide for Monday and we can chat through it at our call Tues:

*Guideline Assets:*
1. lower thirds - can use mustard here as accent color
2. show logo, on box (black and white only)
3. show logo, as bug (black and white only)
    a. horizontal one line
    b. stacked variation
4. on screen reads - can use mustard here as accent color
5. thumbs (these mocks will take us a bit longer as we want to talk through optimization with a larger team on our end, so won't include thumbs for Monday)
6. title card (to be animated, though not in Monday's iteration of the guidelines)
7. end card (to be animated, though not in Monday's iteration)
8.  Youtube banner, (2560 px X 1440 px) - horizontal logo
9. Confession Cards, printed
• Grown By Movember to appear:
    ◦ printed on box
    ◦ logo bug variation
    ◦ youtube header banner
    ◦ end/closing title cards
    ◦ standard logo variations for PR/media assets
• Grown by Movember to NOT appear:
    ◦ thumbnails
    ◦ youtube profile icon
    ◦ Confession Cards

messages.text:
Hope you all had a great weekend :sunny:

We've created a <https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1hvIYSs2MEZ28Y9U91zl1Eb2H_NfKEJwud0REzIOlnbg/edit?usp=sharing|briefing doc for the vox pop experts>. This should help explain the concept to the experts that you've identified for each episode and how they fit in. This is a master version, and each expert should receive a version with just the relevant Confessions to the episode they're going to be in (eg. The expert who is going to give advice on our breakup confessions (ep 3) should only have slide 10 in the briefing deck they receive, and not 8,9 and 11).

Give it a read through and let us know any feedback points or additions. We can chat this through in the call tomorrow, too :handshake::skin-tone-3:

In the brief you'll see that we've used the confessions from the <https://docs.google.com/document/d/1pS0bYAwzh95dVY3JuG63IS7IlXUziznLHMwnvl1uQNE/edit?usp=sharing|Confession Box: Dilemmas v3> document we sent over a couple weeks ago. We can action and chat through Tom's feedback comments on the conversation structure this week, but as there's no feedback on the confessions themselves, we take it that we're all good to run with these :+1::skin-tone-3:

Hi team, we have received feedback from our internal team on the amplification plan. Overall they are  supportive of the approach - particularly liked starting with organic content before the paid approach and suggested channels. We are flagging with our media agency who promote the Movember fundraising campaign given timings so we aren’t bidding against ourselves in programmatic but we think unlikely given target audience.

There was a question from Sam our head of digital and preformance media which would be good to quickly touch upon in our catch up call tomorrow:

"I’ve compared the output based on benchmarks for collaborative platform content we’ve done in the past with talent/partners/brands and publishers. Just a few things to highlight so we go into this knowing the full value exchange from the output outlined in the media plan:

• eCPM estimated markup is *20%* with an actual eCPM of £14.98 based on the guaranteed minimum impressions outlined. This is common, so I went a level deeper to look at cost per reach compared to frequency of exposure to the content below…
    ◦ eCPR, effective cost per reach based on 12.5M reached is £23.96, which is 4.5x the cost of reach from our own channels via paid, so we should consider the value of this audience – is the cumulative impact of seeing this message 4.5x more valuable? Just a useful question to ask given the likely recall from seeing/potentially seeing the content 1.6x may be quite low. 
• Suggestion: Looks like a good spread of publishers/community pages (Archbishop of Banterbury – so good!) which I think is helpful if driving a higher average unique reach than the 12.5M put forward for the £300k investment.
    ◦ Could we put to TNM an approach that drives a slightly higher volume of overall unique reach over the 4/5 weeks in market, to aid recall and ultimately consumption of the content? The only caveat from my side would be – do we have a benchmark for their view through/video completion rates? If so perhaps they can share and I could re-look at the output."

messages.text:
Hey everyone. Looking forward to catching up tomorrow. Thought this was a great article on masculinity and relationships and wanted to share. This is a good summary of what we're trying to tackle.

_Things are really intense when you're young. Sexual rejection is basically an existential experience. This is what makes young boys particularly vulnerable to bullshit artists online and it's why we're willing to erect whole ideological structures on the basis of someone just not being that into us._

_It never occurs to you that someone simply didn't fancy you. Instead, their lack of interest is a rejection of your entire self. Not only is nothing about you valuable or attractive, nothing ever will be. Your character, your physique, your smell, your interests, your disposition, your life chances, your eyebrows - every one of these things have been refused in a take-it-or-leave-it bundle._

_Early rejection therefore sting in a way that it will never sting again. It can plunge teenagers into a pit of self-hatred and savage, knife-wielding introspection. We watch the one we pined over go off with someone else and we feel a desperate sense of need and despair, a challenge not to our good fortune but to our whole sense of identity._

<https://iandunt.substack.com/p/how-to-be-a-man-4ae>

attachments.title: How to be a man
attachments.text: The right's narrative about male attractiveness is grounded in Social Darwinism and free market economics. Can progressives tell a better story?

Hey <@U03KNV84NUB>,

We connected as a team and absolutely love the logo – you’ve nailed it. :raised_hands: One small thing from our side: as we’ve mentioned before, for the *circular YouTube channel icon* specifically, we’d suggest a version with a simpler, singular motif (eg the letter M alone)
The reason is twofold:
• At the smaller sizes where channel icons usually appear, the detail of the moustache might be lost and the full MO:TV wordmark may be too small to be eligible .
• Our target audience (14–18) might not connect as much with the moustache symbol itself.
For the icon, something super simple – either the *M* or a different motif you can come up with – would work best, similar to the examples in the screenshot attached.
Of course, we’d keep the moustache in the *master logo* for other uses (website, press releases, publications) where it signals brand alignment perfectly.

Hello TNM team. We have a favour to ask. On September 29th, we are launching our Young Men and Media Collective-  a "what works" fund and wider learning network dedicated to evolving narratives of ‘what it means to be a man’ that reach young men online.

We are seeking applications to our funding opportunity from organisations who work directly to reach young men online, but also from influencers and creators who have a big youth male audience, and who would be interested in creating content that promotes alternatives to the narrative that young men need to be 'ripped and rich at all costs'.

We are planning to promote the opportunity through our social channels, and also encourage Movember followers to tag creators they think would be a good fit for the grant fund. The team were asking about reaching out to some of the creators from Confession Box. We wondered a) what you thought of this promotional approach and b) whether you had creators as part of your network that you think would be interested in the opportunity, and had thoughts about how we could reach out to them?

messages.text:
Hi all,

We have an exciting company update that's finally out in the open. Our new holding company is called <https://caliberinc.co/|Caliber>.

Caliber is the new home for our agency, now called Caliber Collective, as well as all our existing media brands - The News Movement, The Recount and Capsule. We continue to dedicate ourselves to defining a new era for journalism, reimagining how stories are created, shared and valued.

This is obviously a big milestone for our business that allows us to bring our brands under one umbrella and strengthen our mission. And while this is an important moment for our growth and our prominence in the media industries, I wanted to take a moment to say that nothing changes in our relationship day-to-day. You will have the same team, the same points of contact, and the same commitment to delivering impactful work.

We look forward to growing together during this next phase!

We’re so excited for this next chapter, and thrilled to have you a part of our journey. Feel free to follow us on<https://www.linkedin.com/company/caliberinc/| LinkedIn> and post about the launch. In the meantime, please don’t hesitate to reach out with any questions!

Hi team! It’s Thumbnail and title time.
We’ve prepared *three thumbnail style variations* to try on episode one*.* This lets us:

• *Test audience response in real time* = YouTube allows something called ABC testing, so we can test 3 thumbnails at once and see which is not only earning the most clicks, but is gaining the most watch time, showing both strong CTR and retention. 
• *Pivot fast if needed* = If one option clearly underperforms or engagement drops in week one, we have backup designs ready so we can refresh quickly without losing momentum and pinning our hopes on one option.  
We’d love your steer on:

• *Thumbnail preferences* = Any suggestions/revisions you’d like us to make before launch, and your steer on what you like and perhaps are unsure of. We can then discuss our reasoning or any tweaks using other case studies. Our design process has been steered by some of the UK-based entertainment-first channels that are popular with young men - and that we’ve discussed in the past in our conversations around MO:TV (eg. Channel 4.0, Footasylum, Chicken Shop Date).
• *Title direction* = Our current thinking is that an entertainment/creator-led format strongly tied to the dating confessions theme will work best for both CTR and audience appeal. We’ve aimed to draw our target demographic in with slight shock and awe, making them ask “what’s this about”, whilst also staying true to the content and alluding to the relationship dilemmas.   
So here we go...

Style A  - We think "My Ex Wants Me Back" summarises Confession 3 concisely and also creates intrigue around whether Chris is saying this about _his_ ex. Would love your ideas on other iterations of the "Confession", eg, "She's pulling away", or "Think she's gunna end it"

messages.text:
Hello TNM team

You have the specific feedback on the edit, but one of the overarching pieces of feedback from some of the team here is whether we can edit in a way to increase clarity and credibility.

We have this balance to strike between it being watchable / entertaining & helpful credible and the concern is always whether we’re adding to the noise rather than offering content that genuinely cuts through with practical, credible takeaways.

We've reiterated the strategy internally to the team:
1. We’re not aiming for the audience to go away with precise rules that help them deal with the specific scenarios: the idea is that we have built in a framework that helps people navigate any scenario and they’ll pick this up the more content they watch.
2. We will measure this and get an idea of whether we’ve been clear enough or whether we need to bring this advice out more strongly in future episodes we shoot – we are testing the approach! And we’re not expecting to get it 100% first time.
3. We are over-indexing towards entertainment as it’s most important the audience like the content so we can build an audience – if we go in too educational it’s difficult to come back from this.
But having said all this, clarity of advice is important and we need to take this feedback on board.  We’re giving the audience advice from host / guest / vox pops and it is a lot, so anything we can do to focus the advice and takeaways I think is welcome.

Some suggestions from the content team that I wanted to share:

• Get to the crux first — e.g. in the first scenario, focus on the importance of talking to your partner before the periphery (friend groups etc).
• Highlight when an expert voice is speaking if we are in effect leveraging them as an expert voice (e.g. in Vox Pops) — a super on screen (“Expert says/Expert take”), a tonal cue, or even a playful device could signal credibility without losing entertainment value
• Explore fun “expert cues” — e.g. sound effects, quick overlays, or playful animation when an expert point drops.
• Tighten the edit and focus on the strongest, clearest advice so it feels more focussed....
• Include key points as supers
Not sure all of these are necessarily right (we have to be careful we don’t go against our No BBC Bitesize rule), but I wanted to share to get your views and see what we can explore in the next edit!

Happy to discuss if helpful!

Hey team! We have our 'Mo Show' next Thursday, which is where we invite all the wonderful people who support us to kick off the Movember 2025 campaign :mo:
We'd love to see some of the TNM crew there (if you can make it) so here are some details and the link to RSVP:

_*Movember Presents: Will you join us at The Mo Show?*_
_Calling all facial-hair connoisseurs, enthusiasts and sympathisers... you and a plus one are invited to join Movember for an evening of Mo-antics as we launch our 2025 Campaign in style! Guests attending on the night will receive complimentary drinks, a jumbo hot dog and an exclusive gift for attending._

_This is no-ordinary get together, you can expect a fab night of all things Mo:_
• _Real stories from our legendary fundraisers who’ve grown, run, challenged and possibly embarrassed themselves in the name of men’s health_
• _Get the inside scoop on what's happening in Movember in 2025 (plus your chance to get your mitts on some fab prizes)_
• _Hear from our Mo-experts who will be showcasing where your money goes and how your moustache dollars can impact men today_
_*Event Details*_
_*Date:* Thursday 2 October 2025_
_*Time:* 1900 – 2300_
_*Where:* The Clapham Grand, Clapham Junction. <https://maps.app.goo.gl/sTqvJvxQiKcTMgNN9|Open google maps>_
_*Dress code:* Casual_
_*<https://events.humanitix.com/movember-presents-the-mo-show-25?accesscode=UKLT|Register here>*_

Hi TNM team, here is the info about the YMMC's funding opportunity. If there are any orgs or content creators you work with who you think would be interested in applying (or a team at TNM or yourselves), please do send it on!

Movember and Equimundo are launching a new <https://uk.movember.com/story/movember-and-equimundo-launch-young-men-and-media-collective-funding-opportunity-application|Young Men and Media Collective> and <https://uk.movember.com/about/funding|funding opportunity>.

The newly launched Young Men and Media Collective seeks to support 8 to 10 partners (organisations or individual content creators) to produce and distribute compelling online content that speaks directly to young men, ages 16-25. The goal is to understand what works to engage young men with alternative, healthier messages to the widespread idea that being ‘relentlessly rich and ripped’ is something they should aspire to, at all costs . Through ‘test and learn’ initiatives, successful applicants will experiment with new approaches to telling stories online, generating insights on strategies that effectively engage young men and help evolve healthier ideas of what it means to be a man in online spaces.

Hey <@U07NR2EGMV5> - I love the crash zoom shots - so i don't mean that - i mean half the shots are handheld and half are static on a tripod, so when cutting between the two it's jarring. So for the static shots to have a filter which makes them look less static.
Hope that makes sense! it's something i've had other editors do - where on a static set up shot, in post they add a filter usually called 'motion' and it makes the shot look more hand-held than totally static.

Had a google to find out how they do this, and looks like:
Apply a very light *wiggle or position jitter* to the clip.
In *After Effects*, you can use the _Wiggler_ or an *expression* like:
 `wiggle(0.5, 5)` (frequency, amplitude).
In *Premiere Pro / Final Cut*, use the _Transform_ effect and keyframe small position shifts.

messages.text:
Hey TNM team <@U03FKF668N4>. Thank you for the Movember social recommendations, they were great.

We talked it through with our social team this morning. They are going to generally follow it, but I wanted to give an update plus clarify a couple of things.

*YouTube*
• They think the community post and playlist makes sense
• *Do you have a recommendation on when to post the shorts for each episode in the week of launch?*
• *When will we see the cutdowns just so we can confirm timings?*
• *Can you just remind us of how you want to test thumbnails so we can include this in our brief?*
• *When will you be sending us the video descriptions just so we can include this in our brief?*
• They are going to also test posting the shorts on the existing Movember YouTube - *do you think there's any danger of them posting the exact same creative on both channels - should we get them to adapt it slightly?*
*TikTok*
• They think posting the cutdowns is good idea. Only thing they flagged is that in their experience, less polished creative works better on TikTok so let's just make sure the shorts feel funny, not too polished. 
*FB*
• They don't want to post on Facebook announcing content and targeting parents / alumni / fundraisers as we are planning to do some impact storytelling once the content is live and we have results
• They are going to test posting the shorts to reels as this tends to reach a younger audience.
*Instagram*
• Similar to above - they will post cutdowns to stories and tag creators. 
• They will want to do a launch post on instagram, but would rather not do it as if it's a program 'we're pleased to announce' etc, but rather a super cut with different creators that is quite engaging. *Is this something we could do?*
*X*
• They probably won't post on X as the community we have on there is more around men's health and it's not really our style to share this sort of stuff, but they might experiment posting one of the cutdowns if it's massively outperforming all the rest.
*LinkedIN*
• We won't share a post on LinkedIN, but we are going to write a substack about the project so they will share that. 
• We will likely share this on LinkedIn as part of the impact storytelling phase once we have some impact results.
*Reddit* 
• They think this is a good idea.
• Movember have their own subreddit which we could post on, but they feel we need to be considered about going into others spaces and sharing it. 
• We are going to hold on this for launch but might revisit it once we see how the content is doing and the conversation around it.
I'm going to set up a slack with the social team on it once I've put a brief in with these details - *keen to add a couple of the TNM team so we can just work through a couple of the bits above. Who would it be from your end?*

messages.text:
Hi team,
Tomorrow’s launch day! I just wanted to say how proud I am of where we’ve landed — the final export looks fantastic. I think the colour grade balances really well given the lighting challenges, the conversation feels natural yet meaningful, and the edit is sharp and elevated by the graphics. Huge thanks to everyone for the collaboration - I remember our first kickoff back in spring!

I did spot a small audio blip in the last upload sent over by Justin last night — I’ve fixed it and re-exported below.

One final note before publishing: there are two versions — one with the Movember moustache bug, and one without. I’m not in the status call later as I’m away, but I would’ve raised for a group discussion. My fear is, speaking from my own personal experince, if I see a piece of content branded with a charity logo, I automatically think it’s watered down and the creators are being told what to say. I don’t want 14-17 year olds to feel this new series and channel is “branded” or overly directed, even when it isn’t.

Because this logo would appear across all LOOP partner channels too, I worry it could have a similar effect on Tiktok and IG too - I fear that with the logo bug, this looks like a brand partnership from the first second, whereas we want the conversation around breakups to feel like its been organically featured on LOOPs channels because it’s shareable and starts a conversation in the comments, not because it’s a paid partnership.
That’s just my view — ultimately it’s your call, of course. Whatever you decide, I think the episode speaks for itself and will land brilliantly.

Ep 1 with logo bug: <https://drive.google.com/file/d/1xneI1CXOO4DXjuxzx8sOBSc9kSWBM6WE/view?usp=sharing>

elements.text:
Hi team,
Tomorrow’s launch day! I just wanted to say how proud I am of where we’ve landed — the final export looks fantastic. I think the colour grade balances really well given the lighting challenges, the conversation feels natural yet meaningful, and the edit is sharp and elevated by the graphics. Huge thanks to everyone for the collaboration - I remember our first kickoff back in spring!

I did spot a small audio blip in the last upload sent over by Justin last night — I’ve fixed it and re-exported below.

One final note before publishing: there are two versions — one with the Movember moustache bug, and one without. I’m not in the status call later as I’m away, but I would’ve raised for a group discussion. My fear is, speaking from my own personal experince, if I see a piece of content branded with a charity logo, I automatically think it’s watered down and the creators are being told what to say. I don’t want 14-17 year olds to feel this new series and channel is “branded” or overly directed, even when it isn’t.

Because this logo would appear across all LOOP partner channels too, I worry it could have a similar effect on Tiktok and IG too - I fear that with the logo bug, this looks like a brand partnership from the first second, whereas we want the conversation around breakups to feel like its been organically featured on LOOPs channels because it’s shareable and starts a conversation in the comments, not because it’s a paid partnership.
That’s just my view — ultimately it’s your call, of course. Whatever you decide, I think the episode speaks for itself and will land brilliantly.

messages.text:
Hi team

Wanted to share an overview of topline stats on Confession Box episode 1 and Shorts. Really great to see such good numbers come in over the weekend ahead of our main amplification levers being put into play.

• Total views at present: 16.7k
• Source of views particularly impressive, with 88% (14.7k) coming via YT browse features, meaning the video has organically been fed into users' feeds and recommendations due in part to our high Click Through Rate of 6%
• Our thumbnail tests haven't led to an all-out favourite among viewers, with the top one on 35% and the other two on 32.8% and 32% respectively - indicating that all three thumbnails have performed pretty strongly with the audience
• Average percentage viewed is 28.3% - slightly lower than we'd hoped but could still rise. This appears down to a notable drop in retention 18 seconds - where we've lost 35% of viewers. From that point on though we see much stronger retention, with 35% of viewers remaining by the 5 minute mark
• Total Shorts views across four videos at present: 3,678
• All four Shorts which have been published have the majority of their views (85%+) via the Shorts feed, another sign that YT is considering this content to be of interest to audiences, and placing it into their feeds.
We have Chris posting today (will confirm a time ASAP) and publisher content is due to start going live tomorrow. On this, wanted to check we're on track to have approval on those assets today? One thought from us - the CTA on some content may read as directing viewers to the main Movember youtube channel so think it would be good to update to MO:TV so it's super clear

messages.text:
And this is the comment we were talking about from our evaluation survey from an 18-year-old guy:

_"So I have just watched the video, and I thought it was actually really good. I wasn’t expecting Chris MD to be on the video, so that was a surprise._

_In my honest opinion, I liked the video. This was because the video actually gave a lot of useful tips and information from people who may have went through the same exact things mentioned; For example the feelings after a breakup, and how somebody like I could navigate through it._

_I didn’t dislike anything at all about this video, if I am honest. I thought it was a really good video that can actually come across as an underrated gem for relationships. I honestly would like more episodes to come out of this video series, as I have learnt quite a bit already from just the first Confession box video._

_I thought the host, Ben Hurst, was good. He was playful with the questions a bit and gave it flavour whilst also keeping it serious. The guest, Chris MD, was unexpected to see on the video, but I actually enjoyed Chris and Ben talking through these situations and specific scenarios throughout the video. Chris brought along a bit of banter, whilst also giving his honest opinion throughout the whole video. Overall, I thought Ben was a great honest, and Chris was a great guest to have on the video series._

_I did recognise Chris MD, and I thought to myself, was I on the right video. But I am glad he was on there as it's good to see somebody I have watched previously on a video. I did not recognise the host, Ben, however._

_Both Chris and Ben seemed genuine and real, based on the specific context they talked about on the video. Both of them are likeable people, and they seem really trustworthy because they essentially talk how my mates would talk. For example, bits of banter with serious, actionable advice. Overall, they did a really good job here, keeping it genuine with bits of banter."_

messages.text:
<@U08R6UNDP5W> we have reviewed the Ben interviews, with some detailed feedback per clip below. It would be helpful for us to have a bit more detailed context for content - particularly who the intended audience for the content would be. These topics/questions are important and likely what a broader audience (beyond young men) would be asking, which are  beautifully answered by Ben! But they seem a bit tangental to Confession Box (in that we're modelling positive, strength-based masculinity) we're not really emphasising this in the content to young guys and it's not the core objective. Our strategy with young men target audience in Confession Box is to show not tell around 'masculinity'. Happy to jump on a quick call to discuss?

Detailed feedback/questions:
• where will these clips be living - on TNM IG and TikTok channels? will you be posting a longer version of the interview anywhere? and if so, is the host introduced so we know who she is for context?
• what does TNM team think about adding a end frame to all clips with "Watch Confession Box on @Movember YouTube MO-TV channel" to pull out CTA, and how this sits in the amplification strategy recommendaitons? 
• please remove mention of "men's movement" from all copy, and "anti-feminist" from all copy
• Clip 1 - we're slightly worried about confronting term "toxic masculinity" but feel Ben handled it well - this will be a question on everyone's mind so might be good to address it head on. If we keep clip, should we change caption  copy to "Is the term 'toxic masculinity' counter productive? So much of the convo...."
• Clip 2 - clip is great at explaining what "healthy masc" is - caption copy suggestion edit: "Instead of 'toxic masculinity' would it be more helpful to focus on what '*healthy* masculinity' looks like? We talk to Beyond Equality's @therealbenhurst *about ways to frame conversations around masculinity to be more useful to young men*. Watch Confession Box on @Movember MO-TV YouTube channel.
• Clip 3 - Change caption copy "We ask Beyond Equality's @therealbenhurst if *social conversation* spends too much time highlighting the differences between the genders, and not enough time modelling 'positive personhood'. Watch Confession Box on @Movember MO-TV YouTube channel."
• Clip 4 - Whilst this is an important question and topic around VAWG, we don't think including this and linking it to Confession Box is right for the target audience or strategy of how we are trying to shift outcomes around relationships for young men. Can we please remove this one?
• Clip 5 - keep the question in blue up on screen for longer? felt like it
• Clips 6 & 7 - Ben did a brilliant job on these - great!! defo want Movember team to promote these!!

messages.text:
Hi Movember team,

I know we're not planning on meeting until later on in the week but I wanted to give a quick analytics update and make a recommendation on some optimizations.

The channel is just hit 100k views with 629 subscribers as we approach 1 month of being live on the platform. :tada::tada: It's not easy to launch a brand new channel with no audience, and it's no small feat that the channel has been able to gain this kind of viewership just within a few weeks of going live.

We're not done yet though! Here are a few updates on the last two videos:

messages.text:
Very important information for you all after our call - unsurprisingly the (gross) American tradition of marshmallows on sweet potatoes for Thanksgiving was a marketing push from a marshmallow company...

*Who's to credit — or blame — for topping sweet potatoes with marshmallows?*

"The Cracker Jack company," says Andrew Smith, editor-in-chief of the Oxford Encyclopedia of Food and Drink in America. It put out a small booklet of recipes in 1917 to encourage people to cook with marshmallows. "Virtually all of the other recipes died with the publication of their book, but the marshmallow and the sweet potato one has survived — and has thrived — ever since."

<https://www.npr.org/2014/11/23/365966380/marshmallows-on-sweet-potatoes-thanksgivings-traditions-exposed>

attachments.title: Marshmallows On Sweet Potatoes? Thanksgiving's Traditions Exposed
attachments.text: Thanksgiving traditions can be a bit inscrutable for people who didn't grow up in the U.S., like NPR producer Olly Dearden. He talked with several experts and got some answers to his questions.
